title: Question Words (W-Fragen)
sourceNote: The transcript is garbled and partly corrupted. The question words and example questions are recognisable; one example (ein Fahrrad) is reconstructed from context.
objectives: I can name the main German question words
I can ask questions with was, warum, wann, wer, wen, wie and wo
I can ask with woher, wohin, wie viel, wie viele, wie oft and welche
I can put the question word first and the verb second

expressions.en: What do you do for a living?
Where are you going on holiday?
How much does a bicycle cost?
How many children do you have?
How often do you play football?

patterns.form: Wie viele + plural noun + verb + subject?
patterns.en: How many children do you have?

grammar.title: W-Fragen: question words
grammar.body:
Questions that start with a **W-word** ask for information. The **question word** is in position 1 and the **conjugated verb** in position 2: *Woher kommst du?*

The answer is never just ja or nein.
grammar.ar: كلمة الاستفهام أولاً ثم الفعل المصرَّف ثانياً.

grammar.title: wo, woher, wohin
grammar.body:
These three are often confused:

- **wo** = where (at a place, no movement): *Wo wohnst du?*
- **woher** = where from (origin): *Woher kommst du?*
- **wohin** = where to (direction): *Wohin fahrt ihr?*
grammar.ar: wo = أين، woher = من أين، wohin = إلى أين.

grammar.title: wer and wen
grammar.body:
**wer** asks for the **subject** (nominative): *Wer spricht gut Deutsch?*

**wen** asks for the **accusative object** (lesson 26): *Wen liebst du?* – *Ich liebe Anna.*

grammar.title: wie viel, wie viele, wie oft, welche
grammar.body:
**wie viel** is used with prices and things you cannot count: *Wie viel kostet das?*

**wie viele** is used with countable plural nouns: *Wie viele Kinder hast du?*

**wie oft** asks about frequency: *Wie oft spielst du Fußball?*

**welche** (which) is used here with plural nouns: *Welche Sprachen sprichst du?*

mistakes.why: For the place of origin use *woher*.
The question word is in position 1, the verb in position 2.

lines.de: Ich komme aus Syrien. Und du?
lines.en: I come from Syria. And you?

lines.de: Ich komme aus Berlin. Wo wohnst du jetzt?
lines.en: I come from Berlin. Where do you live now?

lines.de: Ich wohne in Hamburg. Wie viele Sprachen sprichst du?
lines.en: I live in Hamburg. How many languages do you speak?

tip: Make flashcards with the question word on one side and an example question on the other. Think of one personal question for each W-word.

comprehension.q: Which question word asks about the place you come from?
Which question word asks about direction ('where to')?
Which question word asks for the accusative object (a person)?
How do you ask 'How many children do you have?'
In which position is the verb in a W-question?
comprehension.a: In second position, after the question word.

items.q: ___ kommst du? – Aus Berlin. (Woher / Wohin / Wo)
___ wohnst du? – In Hamburg. (Woher / Wohin / Wo)
___ fahrt ihr im Urlaub? – Nach Italien. (Woher / Wohin / Wo)
___ alt bist du? – Dreißig. (Wie / Wer / Wo)
___ Kinder hast du? – Zwei. (Wie viel / Wie viele)
___ kostet das Fahrrad? – 200 Euro. (Wie viel / Wie viele)

exercises.title: Match question and answer
exercises.instructions: Match each question with a suitable answer.

exercises.title: Translate
exercises.instructions: Write the question in German (use du where 'you' appears).

items.q: How often do you play football?

summary: W-questions start with a question word; the verb is in second position.
wo = where, woher = where from, wohin = where to.
wer asks for the subject, wen for the accusative object.
wie viel (uncountable / price), wie viele (countable plural), wie oft (frequency), welche (which).
